## 1. Scope match of the existing half-power theorem
AR-006 explicitly states an exactly-two N2 theorem and cannot alone be quoted as a raw graph bound. Reading Stage14 Final R06, Lemmas3.1/3.2, Proposition3.6 and its final proof fills this scope adapter: E=N2+3T, E<=V B^o(1), V<=B^(1/2+o(1)). Thus E<=B^(1/2+o(1)) on the full raw graph, and P<=E/3 remains valid. No retraction of the existing endpoint ceiling is justified.
Stage14-X13 charges common core, primitive agreement pair and one reconstructed column; reverse reciprocal completion has B^o(1) multiplicity. These complete counts do not contain a new bound for the distribution of c_raw. The old historical cross-root H is not identified with c_raw.


## 2. Reuse the existing R502 family
For coprime positive m,n with 7/2<m/n<4, put
 A=(m^4-n^4)(m^4-81n^4),
 B0=4mn(m^2-3n^2)(m^4+2m^2n^2+9n^4),
 C0=16m^2n^2(m^4-9n^4),
 D1=m^8+46m^4n^4+81n^8,
 D2=4mn(m^2-3n^2)(m^4+10m^2n^2+9n^4),
 D=(m^4-2m^2n^2+9n^4)(m^4+10m^2n^2+9n^4).
Exact identities:
 A^2+C0^2=D1^2, B0^2+C0^2=D2^2, A^2+B0^2+C0^2=D^2. (156.2)
The fixed cone has 0<A<B0<C0; this is the source R502 cone. Divide by g=gcd(A,B0,C0). The primitive cuboid has R=D/g and two integer faces, with no condition on its third face needed here. Divisibility of every diagonal by g follows primewise from g^2 dividing its square.


Let g1=gcd(A,C0), g2=gcd(B0,C0), K=4mn(m^2-3n^2),
 J=(m^2+n^2)(m^2+9n^2), L=(m^2-n^2)(m^2-9n^2).
Then A=JL, D2=KJ. Also
 g2=K e, e=gcd(m^4+2m^2n^2+9n^4,4mn(m^2+3n^2)).
Write b=1 if m,n both odd, else0; a=1 if3|m, else0. Exact formulas are
 g1=2^(7b)3^(4a)<=10368, e=2^(2b)3^(2a)<=36.           (156.3)
These formulas are proved below, not inferred from a finite census.


The two reduced primitive faces sharing the physical C0 edge are
 F1=(C0/g1,A/g1,D1/g1), F2=(C0/g2,B0/g2,D2/g2).
Their cross-gcd factors are c12=gcd(D1/g1,B0/g2) and c21=gcd(D2/g2,A/g1).
Since D2/g2=J/e and A/g1=JL/g1, put u=J/e,v=JL/g1. The identity g1 v=e u L implies u|g1 v, so u/gcd(u,v) divides g1. Therefore
 c_raw=c12 c21>=c21>=J/(e g1)>=J/373248.                (156.4)
This arithmetic inequality survives primitive reduction and measures the actual raw edge, not an ambient parameter lattice.


### Proof of (156.3)
For any p>3, p|m or p|n makes A and the quartic norm factor units modulo p, so cannot contribute. If p does not divide mn and p|C0, then m^4=9n^4 modulo p. The two factors of A become8n^4 and -72n^4; neither vanishes for p>3. Hence g1 has no prime>3.
For e, again a prime dividing mn cannot divide its quartic F=m^4+2m^2n^2+9n^4 unless p=3. If p>3 divides m^2+3n^2, substitution gives F=12n^4 modulo p. Thus e also has no prime>3.
At2, opposite parity makes A and F odd. When both are odd, v2(C0)=7 while both factors of A have valuation at least4; hence v2(g1)=7. Also F=12 modulo16, so v2(F)=2, while4mn(m^2+3n^2) has valuation at least4, giving v2(e)=2.
At3, when3 does not divide m, C0 is a3-unit (if3|n also both A and F are units), and either F is a3-unit or the complementary denominator is, so both minima are0.
When3|m with r=v3(m)>=1, v3(C0)=2r+2. The first factor of A is a3-unit; the second has valuation at least4, and exactly4 for r>=2. At r=1 the C0 valuation is4. Hence v3(g1)=4 in every case.
For e, the denominator4mn(m^2+3n^2) has valuation r+1. At r=1, F has valuation at least2 and denominator exactly2; at r>=2, F has valuation exactly2. Hence v3(e)=2. This proves all claims.


## 3. Count actual primitive raw objects
Set T=floor((B/240)^(1/8)). Take n in (T/8,T/4], and m=4n-k with 1<=k<n/2 and gcd(k,n)=1. Then m,n<=T, 7/2<m/n<4, and m>7T/16. The usual Mobius/totient count on this fixed cone gives >>T^2 distinct reduced parameters.
D<=240 T^8, so R=D/g<=B. Also J>=m^4>=(7T/16)^4, and (156.4) implies c_raw>=const*T^4>=const*sqrt(B).
Primitive reduction identifies at most8 of these parameters per canonical cuboid: the largest-edge/space-diagonal ratio is
 C0/D=16t^2(t^4-9)/[(t^4-2t^2+9)(t^4+10t^2+9)], t=m/n,
a nonconstant rational function of degree at most8. For a fixed ratio, its cross-multiplied polynomial has at most8 roots. The cone fixes the largest edge, and this ratio is invariant under primitive scaling. Thus there are >>T^2>>B^(1/4) distinct primitive raw objects and raw edges with large c. Choosing kappa smaller than the resulting constant proves (156.1).
This argument does NOT need Faltings, the third-face-square exception set, a perfect-cuboid example, or a numerical absence result.


## 4. Consequences for globalization budget
At C=kappa sqrt(B), the claimed uniform upper bound is B^o(1), contradicting B^(1/4). At C=B^gamma, 1/4<gamma<1/2, all these objects eventually lie in the tail while the upper bound would be B^(1/2-gamma+o(1))=o(B^(1/4)).
For the intended C=B^(1/6+eta), the proposed upper exponent is1/3-eta. If eta>1/12 (and gamma<1/2), it contradicts this family; if0<eta<1/12, its exponent exceeds1/4, so this family is compatible with that upper bound. At eta=1/12 the exponents agree, so no contradiction is established.
The R502 family itself is only B^(1/4) in power scale, below the M3 lower benchmark B^(1/3). It obstructs the chosen strong RAW certificate, not P/M3→0. Its presence shows why imposing endpoint/M3 masks matters rather than demanding excessive decay of all exactly-two objects.


The other156 budget choices remain blocked with current inputs: absolute-value/divisor bounds on155.5 return the original moving-R circle envelope and do not supply a global cancellation estimate. A denominator improvement merely above1/3 cannot close using the present half-power numerator; a standalone denominator closure needs an exponent strictly above1/2. No new additive or denominator theorem is proved here.


## 5. Mechanism decision and next task
Correct the previous portfolio recommendation: do not make the UNIFORM raw C-tail the default main attack; its strong version is false. Keep XG-008 identities and the threshold-specific XG problem open for0<eta<1/12, but only reopen it with an actual stratified moment theorem and a small-c/large-tau residual budget.
Next157: test the fixed-finite-inert-prime block relative receiver on exact M3. A sufficient theorem is, for arbitrarily large fixed finite S,
 limsup_{B→∞} M3_accepted(S,B)/M3(B)<=rho^|S|, rho<1,
including bad/zero residues. Fix S before B→∞; then enlarge S. Single-prime marginals alone are not enough. Stage15 M2 congruence asymptotics and ambient parameter CRT do not transfer automatically. The next card must find a genuine physical-measure distribution input or record its missing hypothesis; it must not merely rename this gate.
TI parked;120 retracted;147–149 retained in scope;152/153 retained;automatic curve-degree and same-witness prime escalation remain paused. E_bal unresolved; no closure forecast.

Starting authority and the test


Fresh MAIN, INDEX, RESULT-LEDGER and active T11 ROUTE all designate154. Its complete card is the current source for the missing same-witness correlation gate.152 and153 remain valid sector theorems. The exact unresolved population is E_bal: primitive canonical positive endpoints at R<=B, some prime outside152's S_B, and R/p^v_p(R)>Y_B for every p|R, with Y_B=B^(1/3)/(1+log B)^30.


155 tests whether enforcing154's shared-edge equality itself supplies a quantitative saving beyond151's original joint Gaussian receiver. It proves an exact gluing formula for arbitrary exponents and cofactors, and an exact equivalence for ALL squarefree split R, with arbitrarily many prime factors. The answer is that compatibility removes independently duplicated witness choices, but the completed local tests reproduce the original sphere equation. No new global or negligible-sector estimate follows. This is not an impossibility theorem for using these representations with a genuinely new analytic estimate.


1. Exact shared-edge gluing, uniformly in the cofactor


Write R=p^n q^m h, p!=q split odd primes, gcd(pq,h)=1, n,m>=1, and all primes of h split. Fix Gaussian primes pi,rho above p,q. Set A=bar(pi)^(2n), D=bar(rho)^(2m), and D(h)=product_(l^a||h)(2a+1). A local p-oriented edge has H_p=A G, Norm(G)=(q^m h)^2; a q-oriented edge has H_q=D L, Norm(L)=(p^n h)^2. The edge is a unit at BOTH p and q.


Same positive edge and complementary-diagonal magnitude means H_p=H_q or H_p=bar(H_q). These pairs have the following complete parametrization:


 H_p=H_q:       G=D K,       L=A K;
 H_p=bar(H_q):  G=bar(D) K,  L=bar(A) bar(K);
 Norm(K)=h^2.                                                (155.1)


Proof: A and D are coprime in Z[i]. In the first equality A G=D L, unique factorization forces D|G and A|L. In the second equality A G=bar(D) bar(L), it forces bar(D)|G and A|bar(L). Substitution gives the displayed K and its norm. Conversely every such K satisfies the required equality and norms. Its p/q valuations are automatically zero because gcd(h,pq)=1.


The two branches are disjoint. Otherwise the common H_q would be real, whereas its q-valuations are0 and2m, impossible for a nonzero real Gaussian integer. Norm(h)>0 excludes zero. The shared H also cannot have zero real part, since a pure imaginary integer has equal valuations at a Gaussian prime and its conjugate.


There are4D(h) Gaussian integers K of norm h^2. Thus the EXACT number of signed oriented pairs is8D(h), and imposing positive common real part leaves4D(h), by the fixed-point-free K->-K involution. This counts oriented representations of one edge, not cuboid endpoints or canonical triples. For h=1 there are8 signed pairs and4 with positive real part, regardless of p,q,n,m.


This replaces the false independent product (8D(h))^2 of two shared-unit cofactor lists by8D(h). It is a genuine removal of duplicate choices. However151 already encodes a triple using a SINGLE global H_i per edge. Those original allocations already contain this compatibility. Since D(h)=h^o(1), the displayed compression supplies no new fixed power of R compared with that original receiver. No such asymptotic estimate is imported as a theorem needed for the gluing proof; the standard divisor-size observation is only explanatory.


2. All squarefree split diagonals: full Gaussian local tests equal the sphere gate


Let R be ANY odd squarefree product of split primes. Select three pairs H_i=e_i+i f_i with positive integer e_i,f_i, Norm(H_i)=R^2, gcd(e_1,e_2,e_3)=1, and exactly ONE odd e_i. These are the original edge/complementary-face circles, before imposing the sphere equation. Any original physical endpoint satisfies these conditions. Define


 F=sum_i(H_i^2+bar(H_i)^2)+2R^2
  =4(sum_i e_i^2-R^2).                                    (155.2)


For p|R choose pi above p. Let I_p={i:p does not divide e_i}. For each i in I_p orient H_i by independently conjugating it so that H_i'=bar(pi)^2 G_i^(p), and put C_p=sum_(i in I_p)(G_i^(p))^2. This orientation exists: if p does not divide e_i, one of the two Gaussian valuations of H_i is0 and the other2. All terms H_i^2+bar(H_i)^2 are unchanged by the conjugations.


The FULL local Gaussian condition obeys


 pi^2 | C_p  iff  pi^2 | F  iff  p^2 | F.                 (155.3)


To see this, modulo pi^2 the conjugates of the oriented unit edges vanish, leaving bar(pi)^4 C_p. For i outside I_p, p divides both e_i and f_i: the norm equation implies p|f_i, so H_i and its conjugate are each divisible by pi and their squares vanish modulo pi^2. Also pi^2|R^2. The factor bar(pi)^4 is invertible modulo pi^2. Finally F is an ordinary integer, so conjugation converts pi^2|F to bar(pi)^2|F, and together these imply p^2|F. This reasoning also handles |I_p|=1; such a tuple cannot pass the local test, because its lone G is a pi-unit.


Taking ALL p|R, squarefreeness and the Chinese remainder theorem yield R^2|F, equivalently R^2|sum e_i^2. Since 0<e_i<R, this sum is strictly between0 and3R^2. Its quotient by R^2 is therefore1 or2. Exactly one odd edge gives sum e_i^2=1 modulo4, while R^2=1 modulo4; quotient2 is impossible. Consequently


 [pi_p^2|C_p for EVERY p|R]  iff  sum_i e_i^2=R^2.       (155.4)


The reverse implication is immediate from F=0 and(155.3). After(155.4), primitivity forces |I_p| in {2,3}, and the positive-edge argument retained in153 gives C_p!=0. Thus requiring these two extra witness filters does not change the equivalence.


Equation(155.4) covers ALL squarefree support sizes at once. It demonstrates why multiplying local probabilities is unjustified here: once the local witnesses reconstruct the same global H_i, demanding all the exact tests is precisely the original physical sphere equation. It does not prove those solutions are frequent, rare, or absent. The weaker integer condition p^2|Norm(C_p) used for candidate upper bounds in153/154 is NOT substituted for the full Gaussian condition.


For nonsquarefree R the same modulo-pi^2 argument still supplies p^2|F, but only rad(R)^2|F after gluing. It does not give R^2|F. Hence(155.4) is not silently extended to repeated-prime-power diagonals. Those remain part of E_bal and still require a bound.


3. What the total budget actually says


Let D(R)=product_(p^a||R)(2a+1). There are4D(R) signed Gaussian circle points per edge. Global triples before the sphere filter therefore cost at most64D(R)^3, exactly the old151/152 allocation envelope. Gluing local orientations into one global triple pays this envelope once; it does not replace it by a proved smaller count of successful sphere triples.


155 provides neither sum_(R<=B,R in E_bal) J(R)=o(M3(B)) nor a negligible new physical sector.154's scalar alphabet-cover obstruction is untouched. Its O(B^(1/2)/log B) balanced semiprime upper budget has not been improved. The prime directions must be consistent, but mere consistency is not a new sparse-population theorem.


Decision: the elementary same-witness/CRT bootstrap FAILS AS A NEW COUNTING MECHANISM. Stop generating successive cards that only add more compatible primes or rewrite the same joint receiver.152/153 remain retained;154's firewalls remain retained; global credit stays0 and the main gate staysOPEN. A future estimate of the already-glued sphere population would reopen this mechanism, but another gluing identity alone does not.


4. Concrete alternative: test additive counting on the exact circle population


For odd split R and d|R define the finite exponential polynomial


 A_(R,d)(theta)=sum_(0<e<R, R^2-e^2=f^2 with f>0, d|e)
                    exp(2*pi*i*e^2*theta).


Orthogonality gives the exact labelled primitive positive cuboid count


 N_prim(R)=sum_(d|R) mu(d) integral_0^1
               exp(-2*pi*i*R^2*theta) A_(R,d)(theta)^3 dtheta. (155.5)


Proof: the integral selects precisely sum e_i^2=R^2 with positive integer complementary diagonals. Each e has one positive f. On such a triple any common divisor g of the edges divides R because g^2 divides R^2; it also divides every f_i. The sum of mu(d) over common divisors d|R of all edges is1 exactly for primitive triples, and0 otherwise. Thus the formula preserves primitivity rather than quietly counting scaled copies. Original canonical masks select a subpopulation, so their physical count is at most N_prim(R). One may retain those masks explicitly for an equality on the original population.


This formula is an EXACT ADAPTER, not a new bound and not a claim of novelty. Dropping phases or taking only absolute-value/divisor bounds returns the old envelope. A useful next study must identify cancellation, additive structure, or a separate stronger denominator estimate that changes the TOTAL exponent on the exact moving-R population. Generic random residues or parameter-side CRT estimates cannot be transferred without a theorem on these sparse circles and their endogenous R.


NEXT156=GlobalAdditiveSphereBudgetSelection: compare actual available bounds for(155.5), and the retained denominator's possible strengthening, against the whole-E_bal budget BEFORE constructing another receiver. PASS requires a concrete theorem and a valid adapter whose total cost improves the present bound toward o(M3), including moving R, primitivity and all residual support types. If no such input exists, record that these candidate mechanisms are presently blocked; do not proceed to infinite case classification. No promise of closure within a few cards is warranted.

The written proofs provide the uniform statements.

Removing at most |S_B|=O((log B)^(4/3)) primes does not change this asymptotic. Unique factorization makes the products distinct. ## 4. A genuine all-degree geometric bridge also misses the current budget


Consider the standard cuboid surface X in P^6 with coordinates (a,b,c,u,v,w,R) and equations


 u^2=a^2+b^2, v^2=a^2+c^2, w^2=b^2+c^2,

This is a geometrically integral complete-intersection surface of degree16. Here is the adapter rather than an unsupported degree claim. Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, the four squareclasses a^2+b^2, a^2+c^2, b^2+c^2, a^2+b^2+c^2 are independent in the projective base function field: each has a branch component occurring to odd order in it and in none of the other three. The four monic quadratic extensions therefore have generic degree16. The coordinate algebra is free of rank16 over the edge-coordinate algebra, hence embeds in this generic field and is integral. The four quadrics have codimension4; Bezout gives degree16. For a positive primitive endpoint the full integral tuple is primitive and its maximum coordinate is exactly R. Thus the project's cutoff is the projective height H<=B, with NO favorable rescaling.


Salberger, “Counting rational points on projective varieties”, Theorem0.9(b), supplies for a geometrically integral degree-d surface a collection of O(B^(3/(2sqrt(d))) log B+1) bounded-degree curves, outside which the point count is O(B^(3/sqrt(d)+o(1))). Applying it with d=16 gives

These are insufficient UPPER budgets, not lower bounds on the best possible cover or the true point count.

## 1. Global arithmetic theorem


For EACH prime power p^n exactly dividing R, put m=R/p^n. Then every such endpoint satisfies


 p <= 3 m^2.                                             (151.1)


There are stronger branch conditions. Let r be the number of edges not divisible by p. Then r is2 or3. If r=2, p<=2m^2. If r=3, p^n<=3m^2. In particular, a primitive positive endpoint cannot have R equal to a power of a single prime. This is a theorem about actual integer endpoints, uniform in height and in all possible geometric complexity; it is not an application of149's curve-polynomial theorem.


Proof in Z[i]. Choose p=pi*bar(pi), Norm(pi)=p. Independently conjugate Hi=ei+i fi so v_pi(Hi)<=v_bar(pi)(Hi); this changes only the sign of fi. Norm(Hi)=R^2. For an edge not divisible by p, v_pi(Hi)=0 and v_bar(pi)(Hi)=2n, hence
 Hi=bar(pi)^(2n) Gi,  Gi in Z[i], Norm(Gi)=m^2.
At least two edges are not divisible by p: if two edges are divisible by p, sum ei^2=R^2 forces the third to be divisible by p as well. Let I be the set of these r edges and C=sum_(i in I) Gi^2.


The exact sphere identity is
 sum Hi^2 + sum bar(Hi)^2 + 2R^2 = 0.                    (151.2)
All terms outside bar(pi)^(4n) C are divisible by pi^2. Indeed, a remaining edge divisible by p has both Gaussian valuations at least1; the conjugates of the I-terms have valuation4n; and R^2 has valuation2n. Thus pi^2 divides C. If r=3, there is no remaining edge, and the conjugate terms have valuation4n while 2R^2 has valuation exactly2n. Consequently v_pi(C)=2n.


C is nonzero. For r=3, C=0 would make both entire sums of squares in(151.2) zero, contradicting R>0. For r=2, C=0 gives H1^2+H2^2=0 and its conjugate;(151.2) then reduces to4e3^2=0, contradicting positivity. Finally |Gi^2|=m^2, so Norm(C)<=r^2 m^4. A nonzero Gaussian integer divisible by pi^2 has norm at least p^2; in the r=3 case it has norm at least p^(2n). These yield the stated inequalities. Units are absorbed into Gi; no complex phase cancellation is assumed absent.

## 2. Elementary sparse-power zero-multiplicity lemma


Let S(w)=sum_(j=1)^r d_j*w^(ell_j), with nonzero d_j, distinct integer ell_j, r<=3. At any finite w_0!=0, a nonzero S has zero multiplicity at most r-1. Indeed vanishing to order>=r implies its first r Euler derivatives (w*d/dw)^h, h=0..r-1, vanish. Their coefficient matrix is (ell_j^h*w_0^(ell_j)). Its determinant is product w_0^(ell_j) times the nonzero Vandermonde product_(i<j)(ell_j-ell_i). This forces every d_j=0, a contradiction. Negative exponents are allowed because w_0 is nonzero. Equal exponents are grouped first; cancellations can reduce the number of terms or make S identically zero. This is a universal lemma, not a finite exponent search.

If m=2, their absolute frequencies must agree, their squared phases cancel, and the sole fixed a_i=0. If m=0 the image is constant and all forms share R. ## 2. Pass from projection to a basepoint-free signed polynomial lift


Suppose the map is contained in P=0, and the146 open mask R*product(A_i*q_i*K_i) is not identically zero, where q_i=2R^2-A_i^2 and K_i=R^2-A_i^2.  E_i=(A_i+Y_i)/2, F_i=(A_i-Y_i)/2,

These identities hold globally as polynomial identities, including at excluded parameter values. If R,E_i,F_i all vanished at a complex projective parameter, A_i=E_i+F_i would also vanish, contradicting basepoint-freeness of the original map. Thus the lifted forms have no common basepoint. ## 3. Odd parameter degree is impossible


At a real projective zero of R, sum E_i^2=0 forces every E_i=0; then E_i^2+F_i^2=0 forces every F_i=0. This is a forbidden common basepoint. Therefore R has no real projective zero. A nonzero real homogeneous form of odd degree satisfies R(-s,-t)=-R(s,t); continuity on the real unit circle forces a zero. R identically zero would force all lifted forms zero. Hence every basepoint-free map as above has even parameter degree.


This is a statement about global real/P1_Q parameter maps. It does not exclude all odd-degree algebraic curves, elliptic cubics, positive-genus curves, or isolated rational points on singular curves with nonrational normalization branches. Multiplying forms by a common polynomial does not change the minimal map degree and cannot circumvent the proof.


## 4. Degree two: every nonconstant lift has an identically zero edge

Stage14-t27 gives an exact endpoint compression to one split partition:
N_{1,1}(B)=3P(B).

Therefore if A_{1,1}(B) denotes active reduced trivial-split directions carrying an actual physical completion, then

A sufficient fixed-power theorem for the M3 target is

## 1. Exact trivial-split compression


For a Stage14 raw edge with shared side s and integral space diagonal R, put


g=gcd(R,s),
D=R/g,
C=s/g.


Let


h=(D-C,D+C) in {1,2},


(D-C)/h=alpha*r^2,
(D+C)/h=beta*u^2,


with alpha,beta squarefree coprime.


Stage14-t20 gives the missing-face squareclass


kappa=alpha*beta.


For an M3 endpoint the missing third face is integral, so


kappa=1.


Positivity and squarefreeness force exactly

## 23. Torus double-lift is a genuine second selector inside the principal triple-spin fiber


### 23.1 Exact torus-square criterion


Let

For U=x+i*y in T(Q),


boxed:
U is a square in T(Q)
iff
2*(1+x) is a rational square.


Proof.
If U=(a+i*b)^2 with a^2+b^2=1, then
x=a^2-b^2=2a^2-1,
so
2(1+x)=(2a)^2.
Conversely, if z^2=2(1+x), put a=z/2. If a is nonzero, put b=y/(2a); then
a^2=(1+x)/2,
b^2=(1-x)/2,
a^2+b^2=1,
and (a+i*b)^2=U.
If a=0 then U=-1 and U=i^2.


Thus the square condition on a rational norm-one phase has one exact rational-square selector.
